User Story: As an SDK consumer, I can use provider-specific adapters for Gladia, AssemblyAI, Deepgram, Azure STT, OpenAI Whisper, Speechmatics, Soniox, and ElevenLabs batch/sync transcription.
Expected Behaviour: Adapters implement TranscriptionAdapter with provider-specific generated clients and normalize provider responses to UnifiedTranscriptResponse. ElevenLabs maps unified options to multipart Scribe fields, handles webhook ack mode, rejects unsupported stream input before network calls, and normalizes retrieve responses. AssemblyAI maps unified URL options to generated createTranscript calls, supports EU routing/auth injection, rejects unsupported non-URL input before network calls, and normalizes retrieve/list/delete responses. Soniox maps URL/file inputs to generated createTranscription/uploadFile calls, supports regional Bearer auth, rejects unsupported stream input before network calls, and normalizes completed transcript tokens. Deepgram maps unified URL/file options to /listen params, supports EU Token auth, returns callback request IDs in webhook mode, rejects unsupported stream input as INVALID_INPUT, and uses request history when projectId is configured. OpenAI Whisper fetches URL audio before generated createTranscription calls, maps file/audio options to json/verbose_json/diarized_json formats, rejects unsupported stream input before network calls, and reports getTranscript as unsupported for synchronous transcriptions. Speechmatics maps URL/file inputs to multipart /jobs submissions, supports regional Bearer auth, returns webhook queued jobs, rejects unsupported stream input before network calls, normalizes running/completed job results, lists jobs through GET /jobs, and deletes jobs idempotently. Gladia maps URL options to generated pre-recorded jobs, sanitizes deprecated language_config keys, returns webhook queued jobs, rejects unsupported non-URL input before network calls, normalizes completed jobs, lists jobs, deletes pre-recorded/streaming jobs idempotently, and downloads audio files. Azure STT maps URL batch jobs to generated v3.2 transcription calls, polls status/files/content URLs, rejects unsupported non-URL input before network calls, normalizes completed results, lists/deletes jobs, and manages subscription webhooks. Provider-specific UnifiedTranscriptResponse raw payload types reflect the actual adapter return shapes for synchronous, webhook, list, and polling flows. Speechmatics completed transcript normalization preserves generated transcript extras such as metadata, translations, chapters, and audio events in extended. File-upload adapters convert Node Buffer input to Blob-compatible ArrayBuffer parts before constructing FormData blobs.
Edge Cases: Remote API changes; auth failures; URL vs file input differences; async vs sync job models; provider-specific options may not map 1:1; multipart FormData behavior differs across runtimes.

User Story: As an SDK consumer, I can use streaming adapters for providers with streaming support.
Expected Behaviour: Streaming-capable adapters open provider websocket/realtime sessions, send audio chunks, emit callbacks, and close sessions. Deepgram maps unified and provider-specific streaming options into the Listen v1 WebSocket URL, authenticates with Token headers, normalizes Results/SpeechStarted/UtteranceEnd/Metadata/Error messages into callbacks, captures raw incoming/outgoing messages, sends binary audio chunks, sends CloseStream for final chunks, closes sessions, and rejects sends when the session is no longer open. AssemblyAI maps unified and provider-specific streaming options into the v3 WebSocket URL, authenticates with Authorization headers, normalizes Begin/Turn/Termination/Error messages into callbacks, buffers audio to provider chunk-size requirements, captures raw incoming/outgoing messages, sends Terminate for final chunks and close, supports updateConfiguration/forceEndpoint, and rejects sends/updates when the WebSocket is closed. OpenAI Realtime maps streaming options into the realtime WebSocket model URL, authenticates with Bearer/OpenAI-Beta headers, sends session.update on open, normalizes session/speech/transcription/error messages, captures raw messages, base64-encodes audio append messages, commits final audio, closes sessions, and rejects sends after close. Speechmatics maps unified and provider-specific realtime options into StartRecognition, connects to the regional realtime host with Bearer auth, normalizes RecognitionStarted/AddPartialTranscript/AddTranscript/Warning/Error/EndOfTranscript messages, captures raw messages, sends binary audio, sends EndOfStream on close, and rejects sends after close. ElevenLabs maps unified and provider-specific realtime options into the realtime WebSocket URL, connects to the regional realtime host with xi-api-key headers, normalizes partial/committed/timestamped transcript and error messages, builds diarized utterances from timestamped words, captures raw messages, base64-encodes outgoing audio chunks, sends end_of_stream on close, and rejects sends after close. Soniox maps unified and provider-specific realtime options into the regional transcribe WebSocket URL, authenticates with api_key query params, normalizes partial/final token and error messages, builds diarized utterances from final tokens, captures raw messages, sends binary audio chunks, closes sessions, and rejects sends after close. Gladia initializes live sessions through the generated REST client, honors typed top-level and generated streaming options, connects to the returned or overridden WebSocket URL, normalizes transcript/utterance/speech/translation/sentiment/entity/summary/chapter/audio-ack/lifecycle/error messages, captures raw messages, sends binary audio chunks and stop_recording messages, closes sessions, and rejects sends after close.
Edge Cases: WebSocket auth negotiation; malformed messages; binary chunk formats; provider-specific keepalive/finalize/pause behavior; reconnect not guaranteed; live API contracts can drift from generated local schemas.
